findings.description: PR rewrites the landed text of accepted ADR 0161 in place, mid-bullet, instead of appending a dated amendment section or adding a new decision with `Amends:`.
findings.body:
**Rule:** [`docs/adr/README.md`](https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/1e3453437a82092f1ca31dd74609138bdc496020/docs/adr/README.md#L19-L21) lines 19-21 say:

> An open PR may still edit the decision it adds. Once a decision has landed, a later change appends an amendment section to it (dated, with the PR) or adds a new decision that links back through `Amends:`. It does not rewrite the landed text.

**What this PR does:** Decision 0161 landed in 0fe1bc9 (#294) on 2026-11-11, before this PR's merge base. This PR did not add it, so the open-PR exception doesn't apply. The diff still changes what the decision says, in the middle of the `--full-tree` bullet:

- It replaces "reads the trusted checkout at the measured sha and at `HEAD`" with "at the target sha the gate pinned under the merge lock (`configSha`), never at the main checkout's `HEAD`", and adds the detached-HEAD reason.
- It splices in a new rule: "A context pinning one sha and not the other is refused before any listing".

The change has no amendment section, no date and no PR reference. A reader of 0161 can no longer tell what was decided when it landed from what #327 changed. Other landed decisions were amended with a dated section (0088, 0139, 0164).

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/1e3453437a82092f1ca31dd74609138bdc496020/docs/adr/0161-the-gate-refuses-a-shared-config-core-worktree-and-reads.md#L51-L61

**Suggested fix:**

1. Restore the landed bullet text ("at the measured sha and at `HEAD`").
2. Record the change in one of two ways:
   - Append a dated amendment section, e.g. `*Amendment (2026-11-13, #327): the trusted listing reads at the pinned target sha.*` It should cover: the `configSha` pinning, the detached-HEAD reason, and the refusal of a half-pinned context.
   - Or add a new decision with `Amends: 0161`.
3. Optionally, as 02b3b35 did for 0139, put a short "(see the amendment below)" pointer next to the superseded sentence.

findings.description: The new measureSha/configSha on the complexity 'before' context has no effect: the only complexity implementation (typescript.adapter.ts:495-501) reads files from disk at measurePath and never calls git or nestedPackageDirs, so the comment's claim that git's reads of the main checkout are pinned to the target sha protects nothing. The before count still comes from the main checkout's disk, the gap decision 157 accepts (ADR 0157 lines 36-38).

The comment says "at the gate the two shas are two commits whatever the paths", but the complexity "before" context sets measureSha and configSha to the same targetSha, so the stated reason for always listing the trusted side doesn't hold there.

The detach-`.git/HEAD`-and-restore rationale is repeated in four places: the nestedPackageDirs JSDoc, the configSha JSDoc, the merge-gate.service.ts complexity comment and ADR 0161. AGENTS.md asks for no call-site copies of the seam's docs; keep it in the configSha JSDoc and the ADR, and point to it elsewhere.

process_issues.description: The guards reviewer opened none of the ~40 test files that use readdirSync/readFileSync, because the static Bash lock limited it to Grep and Read, so it couldn't rule out every source-scanning guard. The PR's own gate report shows the full test suite passing at the head, which limits the risk.

The consolidator grouped findings 2 (the complexity before-side pins have no effect, merge-gate.service.ts) and 3 (the 'two shas are two commits' comment, git-tree.client.ts). They are different root causes with separate fixes in different files, so the orchestrator kept them separate and set no merged_duplicates.
